decision: Upgraded the Netflix blog and spec from second-hand to read directly via a text extractor, and that changed the playback answer

decision: Tested Dolby metadata handling through the real CLI on synthetic clips, with a small bit editor because FFmpeg cannot write DRC words
why: Reading FFmpeg docs suggested the constant-gain path was not constant on Dolby sources. A run settles it where an argument would not
evidence: spike/dolby_bits.py, spike/dolby_tests.py, spike/results/dolby_results.json T3 and T4
result: two real bugs reproduced

decision: Checked the bugs apply to real encodes using FFmpeg's public FATE samples, not any personal library
why: A hand-edited DRC fixture only proves the mechanism. Real streams might not carry these fields
result: 6 of 7 carry dialnorm other than -31; default decode changed the audio on all 7; 7 clips say nothing about prevalence

decision: Tested VLC directly instead of inferring from its source
why: A researcher could only reason from source about which decoder VLC picks. VLC is installed here and the test took a minute
evidence: VLC 3.0.24 transcode of the dn31, dn24, drc and nodrc clips; figures in research.md section 5b
result: ignores dialnorm, applies DRC, same as FFmpeg

decision: Threw away the first dialogue fixture run and rebuilt the fixtures
why: F4 and F5 peaked at +4.6 and +6.9 dBTP with a gap of up to 21 LU, beyond the 15 LU the sources report, which inflated every headline spread
evidence: dialogue_spike.py FIXTURES comment; rerun gates in spike/results/dialogue_results.json
result: rerun gaps -3.3 to +12 LU, peaks at or under -0.1 dBTP

decision: Replaced the speech-to-background metric with a per-block median
why: The integrated version read +19 dB on F5 because a few bursts landing on speech ruled the gated mean. That number was an artefact, so it went
result: compression now reads -0.3 to -1.9 dB, constant gain 0.0, centre boost +3.0 to +4.0

decision: Tried trimming loud blocks from the gate; kept the result for stereo and rejected it for the centre channel
why: Trimming pulled whole-mix and stereo worst cases down (5.73 to 1.4 LU, 4.98 to 2.11) but made the centre channel worse (+0.87 to -3.04), because it removes legitimately loud lines. Tuned on fixtures, so only an idea to test
result: centre uses the plain gate; stereo stays low confidence

decision: Reran recipes so at least one runs off the estimate, and added the gap-triggered ladder as recipe J
why: Recipes using the known dialogue level are perfect by construction, so they prove little about a real tool. Recipe F also left high-range films 7 to 11 LU loud, showing compression is still needed
evidence: recipes I and J in dialogue_spike.py
result: see research.md section 5

decision: Ruled out WebRTC VAD for dialogue gating
why: Flagged 81 to 96 percent of music and effects as speech, and 94 percent of the no-dialogue fixture. Published film figures agree (61 percent accuracy, Sharma et al)
result: rejected

decision: Ruled out FFmpeg's dialoguenhance as a stereo dialogue measure
why: Zero dependency was attractive but it read +0.8 to +5.1 LU high, including +5.1 on the easiest fixture
result: rejected

decision: Ruled out source separation as a dependency for now
why: Best published dialogue separation is good, but Demucs is archived and needs about 1.5x the track's duration on the hardware its README describes, with 3 to 7 GB of GPU memory: too heavy for a CLI swept over a NAS
result: rejected for now; noted as the fallback if VAD fails on real films

decision: Ruled out carrying metadata instead of changing the audio as the default
why: FFmpeg and VLC ignore dialnorm by default (tested), mpv disables DRC (manual), Plex is closed, Android's keys are AAC only, and open encoders write no DRC words. Only hardware Dolby decoders apply dialnorm, and which clients reach one is not public
result: kept only as do-no-harm and a client-specific lossless option

decision: Ruled out LRA as the compression trigger, replacing it with loudness above dialogue over 5 LU
why: AES TD1009 and A/85 both reject LRA targets. EBU R 128 s4 gives the 5 LU rule directly. In the fixtures LRA could not separate a quiet drama (15.8) from near-field action (16.6) while the gap did (-0.3, -0.4, then 7.6 and 12). Netflix and Torcoli do use LRA, so sources conflict and the note says so
evidence: quote_check td1009-lra, a85-lra, s4-ldr, torcoli24-lra; dialogue_results.json gates
result: recommendation

decision: Chose dialogue -27 with a -24 whole-programme fallback under 15 percent dialogue over -24 dialogue and -20 programme
why: It is Netflix's published pair and inside A/85's streaming range. Compliant titles need no re-encode, which serves least lossy. -24 hit the 6 dB limiter budget on both high-range fixtures. The open cost is re-levelling files already at -20, which needs real data
evidence: nf-target, nf-fallback, a85-streaming; recipes F and G
result: recommended; the validation task may still pick -24

decision: Recommended against flipping the default now: fix the bugs, measure read-only, validate on real files, then decide
why: All accuracy evidence here is synthetic, TTS over simple beds is much easier than film, and no published test compares an open gate with Dolby's. Flipping now could re-encode a library on an unproven number
result: staged in filed tasks
